title: KV Thermostat — dynamic memory shaping for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a runtime 'KV Thermostat' subsystem that dynamically shapes KV cache residency and prefetching for model-specific memory profiles (Llama-variants, Mistral-variants, Qwen-variants) in long-context configurations (32k–64k). This ticket covers design, implementation, and validation of a lightweight controller that enforces per-model memory budgets, integrates with continuous batching, and coordinates with the slab allocator to reduce fragmentation and OOMs while preserving latency SLOs. Scope: implement heuristics, expose tuning knobs in config, add telemetry, and run cluster-wide experiments on A100/H100 pools.
acceptance_criteria: KV Thermostat can cap KV residency per-model and maintain stable GPU memory headroom within configured target (±5% of target) under synthetic 32k/64k workloads
No increase in 99th percentile token-latency >10% compared to baseline for single-request latency under same load profile
End-to-end integration tests that simulate continuous batching demonstrate reduced OOMs by >= 85% for stress workloads used in prior incidents
Perf dashboards show memory fragmentation metric reduced by >= 20% for tuned models vs baseline
Config knobs documented in Console and runtime-1.22 release notes; feature flag gated for gradual rollout
technical_decisions: Use a token-aware thermostat that estimates expected KV growth per-request based on model and sequence-length histogram instead of naive fixed caps
Eviction policy will be multi-tier: soft-prefetch limit -> LRU-like slab eviction -> coarse-grained segment offload (fallback to disk) for extreme memory pressure
Integrate thermostat with batch scheduler: when budget approaches threshold, prefer smaller batches or fall back to compatible smaller-quantized model variant
Implement GPU allocator hints (pre-reserve slab lanes) to minimize fragmentation; coordinate with existing slab compaction pass from ENG-112034
Expose per-model memory_budget_bytes and prewarm_budget_tokens as runtime-config and Console UI controls
notes: Trade-offs: tighter KV caps reduce OOMs and fragmentation but can increase re-computation and latency for cache misses. We tune for P50/P95 latency preservation while prioritizing availability for high-value customers.
Long-tail workloads (token bursts >32k) will require further evaluation; we will treat these as customer opt-in and provide guidance for dedicated capacity purchase.
We will leverage telemetry from previous memory incidents and long-context heatmaps to seed initial budgets per model.
Will coordinate rollout with Dedicated teams (ticket ENG-760401) to ensure reserved pools can opt-out of thermostat enforcement
test_plan: Unit tests for thermostat controller (budget accounting, decision thresholds, eviction hooks)
Integration tests with continuous-batching harness reproducing mixed-request sizes (1k–64k) across Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants
Scale test on staging cluster (20 A100s): run 72-hour soak with mixed traffic replay and measure OOMs, 95/99 latency, and memory fragmentation
A/B experiment on small fleet (10%) comparing baseline vs thermostat under identical traffic; collect cost-per-token and error-rate metrics
Regression test ensuring feature-flag default is off for older runtime versions
risks: Aggressive eviction could regress quality if key KV entries are evicted prematurely for generative chains
Complex interaction between thermostat and batcher may cause unexpected batching oscillations under bursty load
Model-specific heuristics may not generalize across future variants; need metrics to detect mis-calibration
Mis-tuned prewarm_budget could increase per-token cost due to repeated cache population
